title: Name each export after its own format

blocks.text: The reporting service lets a user pick the format of a report, and `Exports.forFormat(...)` hands back the matching exporter. The files are supposed to be named after their format, but support keeps receiving CSV and JSON reports named `something.dat`, which nothing opens with the right program.

Finish `fileName(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Exports.java`. You may change how the exporters declare their extensions; keep each exporter's extension the same text it is now. When you're done, every exporter names its files with its own extension, however the code that holds it declared its type, including an exporter whose format builds on another one. About five lines in total.

cases.says: the base exporter, and the one picked for an unknown format, name files with .dat
an exporter held as an Exporter names its files with its own format's extension
an exporter that extends another exporter uses its own extension, not its parent's

origin.section: An Instance Method Is Chosen by the Object; a Static Method by the Declared Type

concepts: An instance call runs the override of the object's class, chosen at run time, so behaviour that varies by subclass belongs in instance methods.
